items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: He may be able to place him because he played around a lot subsequently with the guitar player, Eddie Conn, and that general group up there.

ctx.x: Who are some of the people from that era who you think have been, I'm getting off of New Orleans again, which I wanted to stick with, but while we're at it, who are some of the people who have kind of forgotten, we talked about Hutch and Ryder before we ever had the tape machine on, as being one of the ones who's kind of forgotten.

Well a lot of them I guess are so forgotten that I can't even remember their names, but you used to hear, I can say this, there were in my town again in this racing season that brought all these big bands, there were also innumerable little nightclubs, there was a Negro Quarter in the town, and this Negro Quarter had many places that had anywhere from five to seven piece Negro bands, there might have been as many as eight or ten of these. And I don't think I ever went in any one of them and didn't hear guys that…
And Bobby got his trombone player.
